dedupe_keys.name: fire model survey survey sheets for egress and evacuation models buildingexodus pathfinder evacnet4 exit89 simulex steps legion and others with developer availability price and validation references

description: The Fire Model Survey is a long-running online inventory of computer models for fire and smoke, and its egress page is the standard reference list of building evacuation models. It is kept by Combustion Science & Engineering, building on earlier surveys by Friedman and by Olenick and Carpenter. The page separates actively supported models, such as buildingEXODUS, Pathfinder, PANIC and Viswalk, from about thirty archived ones, including EVACNET4, EXIT89, Simulex, STEPS and Legion Studio. For each linked model a survey sheet gives the version, developer, a short and a detailed description, references for the user's guide, technical basis and validation, availability, price, hardware and a contact. The sheets are free to download as PDFs. For several early models the sheet is now the only remaining public description: EVACNET4's download site at the University of Florida no longer exists, EXIT89 was never sold by NFPA, and IES no longer lists Simulex. Caveats: the survey has not been updated since 2015, availability and prices are as the developers reported them then, and no licence is stated. Coverage is worldwide. Simulation uses: choosing and documenting evacuation models for emergency planning, and tracing the lineage of older models cited in reviews. Related records: the PedGo evacuation model (model-traffgo-pedgo) is one of the currently sold egress tools this survey helps place.

schema_summary: List of egress models split into actively supported (buildingEXODUS, maritimeEXODUS, PANIC, Pathfinder, Social Distances, TSEA, TTAM, Viswalk) and archived (Allsafe, ASERI, BFIRE II, BGRAF, EESCAPE, EGRESS, EgressPro, ELVAC, ERM, E-SCAPE, EVACNET 4, EVACS, EvacSim, EXIT89, EXITT, F.A.S.T, Legion Studio, Magnetic Simulation, Myriad II, PEDROUTE, SEVE_P, Simulex, STEPS, Takahashi's fluid model, VEGAS, WAYOUT); each linked model has one or two survey sheets (2001/2002, 2007, 2014 or 2015) with model name, version, classification, short description, modellers and organisation, user's guide, technical and validation references, availability, price, hardware, language, size, contact and a detailed description
